newsitem.title: UK: Britain to quit U.N. industrial group.
newsitem.headline: Britain to quit U.N. industrial group.

text.p: Britain said on Monday it would pull out of the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) at the end of next year.
UNIDO, a Vienna-based arm of the United Nations, promotes industrialisation in the developing world. The group has seen interest wane as budget-conscious governments look to cut costs.

Baroness Lynda Chalker, Minister for Overseas Development, said Britain would withdraw from the agency "from the end of 1997...We will review this decision towards the end of next year in the light of progress on wider U.N. institutional reform."
Britain would save 4.7 million pounds ($7.72 million) a year by dropping out, robbing UNIDO of 7.4 percent of its budget.
In Vienna, UNIDO director-general Mauricio de Maria y Campos of Mexico expressed shock at the decision and said the body had been at the forefront of U.N. reform to cut costs and staff.
"Hitting out at the one U.N. organisation that did most in terms of reform is a powerful disincentive to reform," he said in a statement.
"We did our job and took the lead in the U.N. system. The broader U.N. reform is not within the realm of UNIDO."
He appealed to Britain to change its mind and not abandon the developing world.

"Recent bloodshed in Zaire shows us again how fine the dividing line is between war and peace. Continued support by major industrialised nations to industrial development as a motor of socio-economic growth is the only way to prevent such horrOrs in future," he said.
The British move follows an announcement by the United States last year that it was pulling out of the organisation.
Germany also indicated last month it may do the same but no decision has yet been taken.
Maria y Campos said UNIDO was once again being cast as the sacrificial lamb for the perceived lack of reform in the U.N.
"It is of great concern that the U.S. isolationist malaise as regards development assistance is becoming contagious at the multilateral level," he said.
UNIDO said it had reduced its budget by a quarter, scrapped an entire tier of senior management, and reduced staff by 36 percent since 1993.
While Chalker welcomed the improvements, she said contributors could not support the agency in today's world.

"We are no longer convinced of the case for a separate institution to undertake this work and have therefore concluded that there are higher priority uses of our annual contribution to UNIDO," said Chalker. ($1=.6087 Pound)
